conviction_note: The findings are a set of small offsetting items: a modest beat on the reported Jul-Sep quarter looks likely from FirstCash's same-quarter read-through, the seasonal revenue step and the full SMG ownership, while gold's October crash and the peso reversal weigh on the FY27 commentary. The stock is already down 13% in 20 days and this name has sold its last two EPS beats, so p_up stays near 50 (52) on an abs move of 6.0 (option-implied 7.46 on a 63%-wide spread, history median 2.0). The +0.3 impact_sum and the +0.24 scaled number agree in sign and size.
bar: Consensus FY26 Q4 (Jul-Sep 2026) EPS $0.40 on revenue $422.4M per Earnings Whispers preview (https://finviz.com/news/418562/ezcorps-fiscal-year-end-report-tests-whether-core-pawn-strength-can-outrun-fading-scrap-gains, 2026-11-06); Benzinga shows EPS $0.42 and revenue $427.0-429.7M (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/EZPW/earnings-forecasts). The two EPS figures are close but do not agree exactly, and the revenue figures disagree. The company gives no formal guidance, so every finding is capped small. Prior-year Q4 adj EPS was $0.34 on revenue $336.8M (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/876523/000087652325000095/a2025-q4pressreleaseex991.htm). Q3 FY26 adj EPS was $0.47 against a $0.41 consensus.
positioning_check: Short interest is about 12.3M shares, roughly 20% of float, with 16.9 days to cover at the 2026-09-30 settlement (curvedtrading.com/stocks/ezpw/short-interest via search snippet only, because the page returned 403). Equibles had 12.2M, 19.9% of float and 15.6 days at 2026-08-19 (https://equibles.com/stocks/ezpw/shortinterest). A large part of this is probably convertible-arbitrage hedging of the $230M 3.75% 2029 converts, which are deep in the money at a $11.23 conversion price (about 20.5M underlying shares), so the squeeze risk is smaller than the headline figure suggests. That is my inference, not sourced. Skew is null in the baseline. Put/call open-interest ratio is 1.35 on only 2,079 contracts, and the ATM spread is 63% of mid. Run-up is -12.96% over 20 days and -3.52% over 5 days, and the stock is 20% off its 52-week high. The October drawdown came with FirstCash's -13% on 2026-10-22, when EZPW fell 8.4% in sympathy, and with gold's worst October since 2008.

findings.finding: FirstCash's Q3 2026 release covers exactly EZPW's fiscal Q4 (Jul-Sep). It reports U.S. same-store pawn receivables +12% and same-store fees +11%, Latin America receivables +15% at constant currency, record pawn receivables of $908M, and 'pawn demand remains exceptionally strong'. EZPW's own Q3 (Apr-Jun) same-store PLO was +13% U.S. and +35% LatAm, so the largest direct peer confirms that core demand did not crack during EZPW's quarter. Consensus has EPS down sequentially from $0.47 to $0.40.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Core PLO growth has been strong every quarter. The Q3 FY26 record PLO (+33%) with an EPS beat of $0.06 drew -2.01% (2026-08-05), and Q2 drew -1.67%. Strong pawn metrics have not been bought recently.
findings.why_not_priced: It is public, but FirstCash itself fell 13% on this release and EZPW fell 8.4% the same day, so the market traded the peer print on gold and multiple rather than on demand. If the demand read-through were priced, EZPW would not have sold off with no news of its own. It is only partly priced.
findings.independence: This shares FirstCash's release with the peso finding. EZPW's own Q3 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000876523/000087652326000064/a2026-q3pressreleaseex991.htm) shows the same trend through June.

findings.finding: Revenue model from EZPW's own Q3 release: Q3 FY26 revenue excluding scrap was $362.1M ($418.7M less $56.6M scrap). Last year's Q3-to-Q4 seasonal step on non-scrap revenue was about +7% (roughly $283M to $302.6M). SMG ($43.1M revenue in Q3) is consolidated for the full quarter, and the peso averaged 17.2 per dollar, 8% stronger than a year earlier and at a 2026 high of 16.87 on Sep 4. Together these imply Q4 revenue of about $435-450M against a $422-435M consensus, and EPS of about $0.42-0.46 against $0.40-0.42 after the scrap compression below.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 FY26 missed on revenue by an aggregator's measure ($408.4M constant-currency against $425.8M) and beat on EPS, and the stock moved -2.0%. Q1 FY26 (Feb) moved +4.46. Q4 FY25 (adj EPS $0.34, +36%) moved +1.95.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus at $422.4M is only about 1% above Q3's $418.7M, even though last year's Q3-to-Q4 revenue step was +8.6% and SMG is now wholly owned. If the street had modelled the seasonal step, consensus would sit near $440M. This rests on my own arithmetic and the aggregators disagree on the bar, so it is filed small.
findings.independence: This is an inference from the company's own Q3 and Q4 FY25 releases (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/876523/000087652325000095/a2025-q4pressreleaseex991.htm). FirstCash's +18% revenue and +28% pawn revenue in the same quarter point the same way. It is not independent of the FirstCash finding on demand.

findings.finding: Scrap headwind: the LBMA PM gold price averaged $4,262 in calendar Q3 2026, 5% below Q2 (about $4,490) and below the Q1 record of $4,873. Management said on the Q3 call that scrap margins would normalize toward 15-20% from 26% in Q3 (38% in Q2) if gold did not rise. Q4 FY25's scrap margin was 29%. At about $52M of scrap and a 15-20% margin, scrap gross profit falls $4-7M quarter on quarter, about $0.04-0.06 per share. This is roughly what the drop in consensus EPS from $0.47 to $0.40 assumes.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Scrap margin compression from 38% to 26% in Q3 FY26 came with an EPS beat and a -2.0% move. The market already discounts scrap as transient.
findings.why_not_priced: It is mostly priced. Management pre-announced the 15-20% normalization, and the Earnings Whispers preview says consensus appears to reflect it. The risk is a scrap margin below 15%, since inventory bought at Q1-Q2 gold levels was scrapped at $4,262. That tail is not in a $0.40 bar built on a gentle drift.
findings.independence: The guidance on the 15-20% range comes from the Q3 call summaries (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/ezcorp-q3-earnings-call-highlights-2026-08-06/, 403 on fetch, snippet only). FirstCash's scrap margins held at about 15-16%, a structurally lower level.

findings.finding: Gold had its worst October since 2008, down 6.3% (WGC) to 12.7% (GoldRepublic), and closed around $3,900; the LBMA PM fix was $3,913.25 on Oct 30. That is about 8% below the Q3 average. EZPW's fiscal Q1 2027 (Oct-Dec) scrap margins and jewelry loan sizes are therefore pressured, and the Nov 12 call will carry October and early-November commentary.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no formal guidance history. EZPW fell 8.4% on 2026-10-22 alongside FirstCash's drop as gold fell below $4,100, so the stock trades on gold.
findings.why_not_priced: It is largely priced. The stock is down 13% over 20 days in step with gold. What is not yet seen is management's quantification of the scrap-margin and loan-size impact for Q1 FY27. Shrunk for the 20%-of-float short interest.
findings.independence: World Gold Council October commentary (https://www.gold.org/goldhub/research/gold-market-commentary-october-2026) and 24/7 Wall St, 2026-10-24 (https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/10/24/gold-just-fell-below-4000-after-its-worst-week-in-five-months/).

findings.finding: The peso reversed after the quarter. It averaged 17.2 per dollar in Jul-Sep (8% favorable year on year, per FirstCash), but FirstCash said on Oct 22 that it was back to about 18.3, equal to last year's rate, and other reports put it at 18.6-18.8 in October. That removes the LatAm FX tailwind for FY27 commentary. LatAm was EZPW's fastest-growing segment, with contribution +56% in Q3.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no specific history for this line. LatAm strength was the highlight of the Q3 print, which still drew -2.0%.
findings.why_not_priced: It is public through FirstCash's outlook, so it is mostly priced. It reaches EZPW only through FY27 commentary, which the company does not formalise. Netted against the rest of the company: U.S. pawn, about two-thirds of PLO, is unaffected.
findings.independence: Trading Economics peso reports (https://tradingeconomics.com/mexico/currency/news/594089). This shares FirstCash's release with the demand finding.

findings.finding: The $230M 3.75% 2029 convertible notes (conversion price $11.23, about 20.5M underlying shares, already counted in the 83.4M diluted share count) become redeemable by EZPW from 2026-12-21. A redemption or settlement plan announced with the fiscal year-end results, for example cash for principal, would cut diluted shares by about 8M (about 10%) and is EPS-accretive.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no prior instance on this note. EZPW refinanced in March 2025 by issuing $300M of 7.375% 2032 notes.
findings.why_not_priced: Nothing has been announced. Cash fell to $311M after the SMG debt payoff, so the funding route is open. Whether management uses the year-end call to address the call date is speculative. The question here is what the money buys: share-count reduction, which is a positive or a zero.
findings.independence: None. The Q3 release shows cash of $311.0M and long-term debt of $519.5M (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000876523/000087652326000064/a2026-q3pressreleaseex991.htm). There is no announcement.

findings.finding: This is the first full quarter with SMG wholly owned. EZPW went from about 74.6% effective ownership earlier in the year to 97.4% in Q3 and 100% in July 2026, so all of SMG's segment contribution ($5.9M in Q3) flows to EZPW shareholders and the minority-interest drag disappears.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no history. This is new to this quarter.
findings.why_not_priced: It is small and probably in consensus already (the Earnings Whispers preview flags it). It is filed because a sell-side model still on a ~97% minority share would understate attributable EPS by under a cent.
findings.independence: Earnings Whispers preview (https://finviz.com/news/418562/ezcorps-fiscal-year-end-report-tests-whether-core-pawn-strength-can-outrun-fading-scrap-gains). This shares the Q3 release with the revenue-model finding.

findings.finding: Insider selling into the summer high: the Chief Legal Officer sold 30,000 shares at about $34.77 on 2026-08-24 under a 10b5-1 plan (a 20% cut to her holding), and a director sold 10,000 at about $35.54 in July. There were no insider purchases in 90 days.
findings.why_not_priced: It is public, and as a 10b5-1 sale it carries little information.
findings.independence: EDGAR submissions list a Form 144 on 2026-08-24 and a Form 4 on 2026-08-25 (https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK0000876523.json).

findings.finding: Canaccord Genuity kept its Buy rating and raised its target to $45 from $44 on 2026-10-15, just before the October drawdown. Per an August snapshot, the sell side has 5 analysts with targets of $36-45 against a $28.48 spot.
findings.why_not_priced: This is wire copy and priced. It records that the sell side was not cutting into the drop, so the bar was not lowered after gold fell. The same page also shows a conflicting $36 note, so the target is unconfirmed.
findings.independence: Simply Wall St narrative on raised targets (https://simplywall.st/narratives/ovuqjd0e-analysts-lift-price-target-for-ezcorp-amid-improved-execution-and-business-model-enhancements).

findings.finding: Reaction function in the group: FirstCash beat on EPS ($2.68 against $2.63) and revenue ($1.10B against $1.07B), raised its dividend 10%, and still fell 13% on 2026-10-22. EZPW fell about 8-10% in sympathy with no news of its own. The pawn group is selling beats while gold falls.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: EZPW's last two beats drew -2.01% and -1.67%.
findings.why_not_priced: The derating has already happened. After a 13% drop the bar for a positive reaction is lower, which is why this is sized near zero rather than as a clean negative.

outside_window.finding: The 2029 convertible notes become redeemable from 2026-12-21. If no plan is announced on Nov 12, the actual redemption notice falls after the window.

baseline_tension: The modest positive tilt on the reported quarter cuts against the -13% 20-day run-up and the 1.35 put/call open-interest ratio. Both are mostly explained by gold's October crash and FirstCash's sympathy drop, which are forward items. p_up is therefore held at 52, not higher.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (beats sold, -2.0 and -1.7 on the last two beats): FirstCash demand read-through cut from +0.5 to +0.4, and the revenue-model inference from +0.6 to +0.4.
Lesson 7 (about 20% of float short, 16.9 days to cover): gold-October negative shrunk from -0.4 to -0.3 and peso from -0.3 to -0.2. The convert-hedge caveat keeps the shrink modest.
Lesson 3 (own caveat): the FirstCash-reaction positioning finding was cut from -0.2 to -0.1, since its own text says the derating already happened.
Lesson 4 (financing is a question): the convert redemption is signed positive because it buys share-count reduction, but it is cut from +0.3 to +0.2 because it is not announced.
Lesson 6 (bar from two sources that do not agree exactly, no company guide): all findings were kept at or below 0.4. p_up, abs_move_pct and print_vs_bar_pct are unchanged.
